nodes.label: app_data_store Group Restructure (Separation of Concerns)
nodes.rationale: app_data_store bundled DynamoDB FullAccess with Textract and SecretsManager, so removing jejen205 to cut DynamoDB access would also cut unrelated Textract/SecretsManager work he actually used. Splitting the two concerns into a new doc_secrets group narrowed DynamoDB access to kimps alone while preserving both users' existing duties.

nodes.label: delete-user Requires Detaching Directly Attached Policies
nodes.rationale: Clearing groups, access keys and SSH keys is not enough: managed and inline policies attached directly to the user also block delete-user with DeleteConflict. Checking only group membership leaves the deletion half-done.
nodes.norm_label: delete-user requires detaching directly attached policies

nodes.label: lookup-events 90-Day Limit + IAM Events Live in us-east-1
nodes.rationale: The Event history API is capped at 90 days regardless of trail S3 retention, and IAM is global so events land in us-east-1. Querying from the account default region ap-northeast-2 silently returns zero results, which reads as 'no events' rather than 'wrong region'. Older history requires downloading raw gzip logs from the trail bucket.
nodes.norm_label: lookup-events 90-day limit + iam events live in us-east-1

nodes.label: Filter on requestParameters.userName, Not userIdentity
nodes.rationale: A plain string grep for an account name matches every event that user performed (userIdentity.arn), producing large numbers of unrelated hits. Only requestParameters.userName identifies the account that was acted upon.

nodes.label: Routine IAM Changes Performed by Root Account
nodes.norm_label: routine iam changes performed by root account

nodes.label: production_dr_runn_hist Is Structurally Append-Only
nodes.rationale: The runnHist/insert.ts resolver uses PutItem with an attributeExists:false condition so only new keys are accepted, and no updateRunnHist/deleteRunnHist exists in the GraphQL schema. Modification and deletion of existing GPS records are therefore impossible by design, not merely unused.

nodes.label: Single Shared AppSync API_KEY (No Per-Field Authorization)
nodes.norm_label: single shared appsync api_key (no per-field authorization)

nodes.label: agent-toolkit Writes to the macOS User Account, Not the Project
nodes.rationale: aws configure agent-toolkit mutates ~/.claude.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, ~/.gemini/settings.json and installs skills under ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills, so every project opened by this macOS user inherits aws-mcp. The toolkit's rules/aws-agent-rules.md was kept in a separate wiki file rather than overwriting the repo CLAUDE.md, to preserve the protected-resources absolute rules.
nodes.norm_label: agent-toolkit writes to the macos user account, not the project

nodes.label: Location Data DynamoDB TTL Auto-Purge Rediscovery (2026-07-20)
nodes.norm_label: location data dynamodb ttl auto-purge rediscovery (2026-07-20)

nodes.label: 7-Day TTL Policy (created_at + 86400*7)
nodes.rationale: All four location tables' insert resolvers stamp ttl = now + 7 days at PutItem time, so DynamoDB deletes records automatically. Whether the 7 days was a deliberate privacy control or an incidental operational-cleanup number is unknown; only the code is evidence.

nodes.label: TTL Under-Retention Finding and Unreleased Fix (2026-07-20)
nodes.norm_label: ttl under-retention finding and unreleased fix (2026-07-20)

nodes.label: Use/Provision Confirmation Data Minimum-Retention Requirement
nodes.rationale: Location Information Act art.23 exempts art.16(2) confirmation records from immediate destruction, and the examiner demanded evidence older than six months. The screenshot submitted in the first round identifies production_dr_runn itself as that confirmation record, so the table faces a retention floor that runs opposite to the one-year ceiling on personal location data.

nodes.label: Phase 0-9 Privatization Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Ordered by four principles: observe first, additive changes first, easily reversible first, and irreversible public-access removal only after 100% of consumers have migrated.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — VPC Flow Logs Observability
nodes.rationale: Nobody knows which clients currently connect to RDS, so any migration without measurement is guesswork. One Flow Logs enablement answers both Q1 (read1 unknown connections) and Q3 (spd-test EIP whitelisting) and is reversible with a single delete.

nodes.label: Phase 3 — Developer Access Path (Hard Gate)
nodes.rationale: After Phase 7 the ms_codegen, ps_path, ps_jupyter and mysqldump workflows all die. SSM port forwarding is the default because every developer already has an IAM user and all tools are local CLIs; Client VPN's $73/month fixed cost is only justified if non-IAM users must reach the DB, and a bastion would recreate the inbound-22 problem being removed.

nodes.label: Phase 5 — Migrating 145 Lambdas Into the VPC
nodes.rationale: Largest workload and highest risk. ms_sam only reads template.yaml, so there is no single injection point; the chosen lever makes the VPC identifier live in one SSM parameter, the logic in ms_sam, and per-repo work a mechanical codemod plus a dependency bump. A CFN Macro was rejected because the templates already carry two transforms.
nodes.norm_label: phase 5 — migrating 145 lambdas into the vpc

nodes.label: Phase 7 — RDS Public Access Removal (Only Downtime Window)
nodes.rationale: ENI reconfiguration plus DNS switch severs existing connections for tens of seconds to minutes. Ordered dev-mshuttle, spd-test, read1, then the protected production writer last, each at least three days apart and each gated on seven consecutive days of zero external srcaddr in Flow Logs.
nodes.norm_label: phase 7 — rds public access removal (only downtime window)

nodes.label: Augment Default VPC With Private Subnets (Not a New VPC)
nodes.rationale: EFS can hold mount targets in only one VPC, so moving to a new VPC would force destructive delete-and-recreate on a protected resource; the 2017-AMI EC2 has no SSM and no documentation and is not reproducible. Adding subnets to the default VPC is purely additive and fully reversible. The 'default' attribute belongs only to the four pre-created subnets, so newly created subnets are unaffected by it.
nodes.norm_label: augment default vpc with private subnets (not a new vpc)

nodes.label: Exposure Cause Is PubliclyAccessible=true, Not Public Subnets
nodes.rationale: An ENI without a public IP is unreachable from the internet even with an IGW route, so the risky, downtime-bearing subnet-group move can be separated from the actual security win and deferred to an optional Phase 9.
nodes.norm_label: exposure cause is publiclyaccessible=true, not public subnets

nodes.label: RDS Split-Horizon DNS
nodes.rationale: Because the default VPC has DNS support and hostnames enabled, an RDS FQDN resolves to a private IP inside the VPC and a public IP outside. Hardcoded host strings therefore keep working after privatization, which decouples 'replace hostnames' from 'remove plaintext passwords' and sharply reduces migration scope.

nodes.label: Secrets Baked Into Bundles at Build Time
nodes.rationale: secret.cjs reads Secrets Manager into .env.<stage> and webpack BannerPlugin inlines the values at the top of the bundle, with zero runtime Secrets Manager calls. Three consequences: rotating a secret propagates nothing without a full rebuild and redeploy, a Secrets Manager interface endpoint is unnecessary (~$19/month saved), and plaintext production credentials persist in every historical artifact in the ms-sam S3 bucket.
nodes.norm_label: secrets baked into bundles at build time

nodes.label: Four Duplicate CloudFormation Stack Names
nodes.rationale: The same stack is deployed from two or more source locations, so adding VpcConfig to the new repo is silently reverted whenever someone deploys the old monorepo. If that happens after privatization the affected Lambda loses its database.

nodes.label: NAT Gateway Is Mandatory
nodes.rationale: 34 backend repos depend on axios/@slack/webhook and call external SaaS (NHN Toast SMS, Kakao AlimTalk, Slack, FCM, OAuth, Channel.io, Notion), so private-subnet Lambdas cannot function without egress.

nodes.label: spd-test Chain Stop/Delete Decision
nodes.rationale: 97.6% idle over 14 days, but it is the only one of the four RDS instances with a fixed service-managed EIP, which itself suggests an external partner may have whitelisted the address. That question must be resolved before Phase 7 touches it.

nodes.label: Hardcoded AWS Access Keys in cron_serv / driver-runn-cron
nodes.rationale: Owners identified by searching the literal key IDs: kimps, fart86 and an 'email' account. fart86 holds AdministratorAccess and its key drives the location-data nightly export pipeline, so a leak would compromise the whole account. Standard fix is switching to Lambda execution roles.
nodes.norm_label: hardcoded aws access keys in cron_serv / driver-runn-cron

nodes.label: Remove Unused Geo Fields From RunnUpdateInput
nodes.rationale: Nothing exploits the field today, but the shared API_KEY means there is no per-field authorization, so leaving it open is unnecessary attack surface. Removing it lets the schema itself guarantee 'location data is read-only', which also helps the OPA argument.
nodes.norm_label: remove unused geo fields from runnupdateinput

nodes.label: DynamoDB Location Data Encryption (OPA Response, Closed)
nodes.norm_label: dynamodb location data encryption (opa response, closed)

nodes.label: Delete by Stack Unit, Never Individual Resources
nodes.rationale: Adopted after the 2026-07-02 accidental DynamoDB deletion: deleting individual functions or resources instead of running delete-stack is what caused CDK-managed tables to be destroyed.
nodes.norm_label: delete by stack unit, never individual resources

nodes.label: Append-Only jq Pipeline for FunctionAssociations
nodes.rationale: update-distribution replaces the whole config, so any existing association omitted from the payload disappears. The pipeline only appends, never overwrites, protecting admin-fe-response-* associations. It deliberately does not dedupe, so already-attached distributions must be excluded from the loop by the pre-check table.

nodes.label: Full Distribution Config + ETag Backup Before Update
nodes.norm_label: full distribution config + etag backup before update

nodes.label: Runbook: RDS Storage Shrink via dump/restore Swap
nodes.rationale: RDS storage can only grow, so shrinking requires building a smaller instance and moving the data into it.
nodes.norm_label: runbook: rds storage shrink via dump/restore swap

nodes.label: Rename-Swap Cutover
nodes.rationale: Renaming old to -old and new to the original identifier keeps the endpoint FQDN unchanged so applications need no config change; DNS repoints within roughly 60 seconds. Matching the master password to the old one beforehand is what makes the swap transparent.

nodes.label: Runbook: WAF Bot Control Rule Toggle
nodes.norm_label: runbook: waf bot control rule toggle

nodes.label: --target Defaults to all (dev + prod) Hazard
nodes.rationale: Omitting --target disables the production ACL alongside dev, so the target must always be named explicitly.

nodes.label: Automatic Full-ACL Backup Before Disable
nodes.rationale: UpdateWebACL is a LockToken-based wholesale replacement and AWS provides no rollback, so the JSON snapshot in backups/waf-acl/ is the only restore path. Deleting that folder destroys the ability to re-enable.

nodes.label: Five-Point Registration for a New Service Monitor
nodes.rationale: Neither the notifiers nor the routing layer discovers monitors automatically, so a new service must be wired into infra-monitor/<svc>.ts, types.ts, infra-monitor/index.ts, server.ts serviceMonitors, and both notifier formatters.
nodes.norm_label: five-point registration for a new service monitor

nodes.label: dry-run by Default, --confirm to Mutate
nodes.rationale: Splitting destructive scripts into report-then-execute prevents a mistaken invocation from destroying a production ACL. status stays read-only; every mutation sits behind --confirm.

nodes.label: AWS Operation History Is the Wiki's Primary Asset
nodes.rationale: The repo's real value is the record of what was done to account 306331009209 and with which commands; the Fastify+cron app is only tooling built on top. Commands that were not preserved are marked with a TODO question rather than guessed at.
nodes.norm_label: aws operation history is the wiki's primary asset

nodes.label: docs/ Retired — llm-wiki Is the Single Source of Truth
nodes.rationale: Keeping the same material in docs/ and the wiki guarantees one copy goes stale and the two diverge.
nodes.norm_label: docs/ retired — llm-wiki is the single source of truth

nodes.label: WAF / Security Hub / Config Must Stay Enabled
nodes.rationale: The account was frozen on 2024-12-28 and AWS required these services to remain active as a condition of release; disabling them risks another freeze. Cost-reduction reviews must therefore never recommend turning them off. Removing only the Bot Control managed rule stays inside the permitted scope.
nodes.norm_label: waf / security hub / config must stay enabled

nodes.label: Keep the 5-Minute Single Datapoint
nodes.rationale: CloudWatch publish lag can leave the window empty and the code falls back to value 0, making 'real zero' indistinguishable from 'no data'. Accepted because the 30-minute cadence means a missed tick is caught on the next one; revisit only when a single missed alert becomes unacceptable.

nodes.label: Send to Every Configured Channel
nodes.rationale: Rather than enforce a single channel-of-record, getActiveNotifiers fires everything that isConfigured. Per-environment selection then reduces to which env vars are filled. A complaint about duplicate alerts would require changing this behavior itself.

nodes.label: Thresholds Hardcoded, Not Env-Driven
nodes.rationale: All environments use the same thresholds, so extracting them to env would add abstraction cost with no benefit.

nodes.label: Scheduler Starts With the Server (No Off Switch)
nodes.rationale: Running cron inside the server process avoids a separate daemon and keeps stop management to a single PID. Side effect: local yarn dev also starts it, so a populated .env fires real alerts during development.
nodes.norm_label: scheduler starts with the server (no off switch)

nodes.label: bus_factor: 1
nodes.rationale: Effectively one person knows this repo's intent, history and operational context, which is precisely why the wiki matters. Unknowns must be left as #todo rather than interpreted.

nodes.label: Hardcoded Seoul-Region Price Model
nodes.rationale: Unit prices live as literals in waste.ts PRICE and are not tracked automatically, so AWS price changes require a manual code sync.

nodes.label: No Queue, No Retry, No Rate Limiting
nodes.rationale: Designed as simple fire-and-forget notification. A failed send waits for the next cron tick; reliability work is deferred until someone actually requires it.
nodes.norm_label: no queue, no retry, no rate limiting

nodes.label: Security Findings Deliberately Excluded
nodes.rationale: The script's doc-comment states that PubliclyAccessible and default-SG rules are excluded as policy-forbidden, so the tool covers only operational and cost dimensions.

nodes.label: UpdateWebACL Field-Preservation Risk on SDK Upgrade
nodes.rationale: The script explicitly re-sends a fixed list of WebACL fields. If AWS SDK v3 adds a new field to the WebACL type, the Update call omits it and silently overwrites it, so SDK upgrades require review.
nodes.norm_label: updatewebacl field-preservation risk on sdk upgrade

nodes.label: RDS rename + waiter NotFound Pitfall
nodes.rationale: AWS briefly returns NotFound while a rename is processing and the standard waiter fails immediately without retrying. A real incident cost 3-4 minutes of read-endpoint outage. Production work needs a hand-written polling loop that treats NotFound as retryable; the same applies to modify-db-instance --no-publicly-accessible in Phase 7.

nodes.label: Split-Horizon DNS Means Host Strings Survive Privatization
nodes.norm_label: split-horizon dns means host strings survive privatization

nodes.label: ms_sam Bakes Secrets at Build Time
nodes.norm_label: ms_sam bakes secrets at build time

nodes.label: ms_sam Validates Parameters Bidirectionally
nodes.rationale: base-generator.cjs checks both that every template parameter exists in config and that every config parameter exists in the template. Adding SubnetIds/SecurityGroupIds to mssam.config.cjs without matching Parameters and Globals.Function.VpcConfig in template.yaml fails the deploy on the spot, which forces the Phase 5 change to be scripted as a codemod across 67 templates.

nodes.label: WAF Metric Dimension Mismatch (REGIONAL vs GLOBAL)
nodes.rationale: monitorWAF lists REGIONAL Web ACLs but getMetricData hardcodes Region: GLOBAL, which is the CloudFront-scope dimension. The metric comes back empty and always reports 0, so WAF alerts may never have fired for reasons unrelated to the threshold.
nodes.norm_label: waf metric dimension mismatch (regional vs global)

nodes.label: 5-Minute Single Datapoint Falls Back to Zero
nodes.norm_label: 5-minute single datapoint falls back to zero

nodes.label: stopped EC2 Savings Counted as Zero Everywhere
nodes.rationale: findStoppedEC2 hardcodes 0 on the comment that EBS is counted separately, but findUnattachedEBS only catches volumes with status available. A stopped instance's root volume stays attached, so it falls through both collectors and the monthly EBS charge never appears in the report total.
nodes.norm_label: stopped ec2 savings counted as zero everywhere

nodes.label: CloudTrail lookup-events: 90 Days and us-east-1 for IAM

nodes.norm_label: aws configure agent-toolkit has account-global side effects

nodes.norm_label: update-distribution is a full put-style replacement

nodes.norm_label: kms 30-day pending window is the only safety net

nodes.norm_label: lambda@edge origin functions live in us-east-1

nodes.label: Read Replica Storage Cannot Be Smaller Than Source
nodes.norm_label: read replica storage cannot be smaller than source

nodes.label: AppSync updateRunn Exposes Unused Geo Update Fields
nodes.rationale: 'Not used today' is not the same as 'structurally blocked'. runn_hist is genuinely safe because of the attributeExists:false PutItem condition; production_dr_runn merely lacks a caller.
nodes.norm_label: appsync updaterunn exposes unused geo update fields

nodes.label: Location Tables Have No Field-Level Encryption
nodes.rationale: Changing SSE from an AWS-owned key to KMS can silently break the nightly S3 export and Streams consumers if their IAM roles lack kms:Decrypt, so consumer permissions must be verified before the switch.
nodes.norm_label: location tables have no field-level encryption

nodes.label: Managed Flink Directly Subscribes to the Location Streams
nodes.norm_label: managed flink directly subscribes to the location streams

nodes.label: driver-tracking-api-production Is Permanently Drifted
nodes.rationale: Auto Scaling plus a legacy capacity cron change throughput live while the CDK template remembers static values, so the live stack always shows drift. The initial fear that deploying would reset capacity was wrong: CloudFormation diffs previous template against new template, not against live state, so untouched properties are excluded from the update. cdk diff answers 'what will actually change' more directly than detect-stack-drift, which only says 'something differs'.

nodes.label: Code Defaults Are the Truth, Not .env.example
nodes.rationale: .env.example and the actual code defaults disagree, and the server boots without a .env at all, so the code defaults are authoritative.
nodes.norm_label: code defaults are the truth, not .env.example
